short: The mathematics of vectors, matrices, and linear transformations that underlies almost all neural network computation.
eli5: The rulebook for moving, stretching, and combining lists and grids of numbers all at once.
example: Running an entire Transformer layer in one GPU operation using matrix math.

short: An ordered list of numbers representing a point or direction in multi-dimensional space.
eli5: A set of coordinates—like GPS latitude, longitude, and altitude—that places an idea or object on a map.
example: Representing a user profile as [age, clicks_per_day, avg_spend].

short: Combining two grids of numbers by taking dot products of rows and columns to transform data through model weights.
eli5: A giant calculator shortcut that mixes hundreds of ingredients into new recipes in one synchronized step.
example: Multiplying an input token embedding by a weight matrix to compute query vectors in attention.

short: Multiplying matching entries of two vectors and summing them to measure alignment and magnitude.
eli5: Scoring how much two arrows point in the same direction—big positive score if they agree, zero if perpendicular.
example: Computing raw attention compatibility scores between a Query vector and Key vectors.

short: A measure of similarity between two vectors based on the angle between them, ignoring their overall length.
eli5: Checking if two compasses point in the same direction, regardless of how big each compass is.
example: Ranking documents in a vector database by how closely their embeddings align with a search query.

short: A mathematical function that assigns a likelihood to every possible outcome of a random event, summing to 1.
eli5: Dividing 100% of a pie across all possible guesses to show which outcomes are likely and which are rare.
example: An LLM assigning 62% to 'cat', 18% to 'dog', and 20% across other vocabulary words.

short: A rule for updating the probability of a hypothesis as new evidence arrives.
eli5: Changing your mind about whether it will rain after you step outside and see dark clouds.
example: Updating the chance an email is spam after observing suspicious phrases like 'claim prize'.

short: A function that converts raw model scores (logits) into positive probabilities that sum cleanly to 1.
eli5: Turning messy judge scores like [5, 2, -1] into clean percentages like [95%, 4.7%, 0.3%].
example: Transforming an LLM's final vocabulary logits into next-token sampling probabilities.

short: A loss function measuring how far a model's predicted probability distribution is from the true target distribution.
eli5: A penalty score that stays tiny when the model bets heavily on the right answer and spikes sharply when it is confidently wrong.
example: Training a language model to minimize surprise on the actual next token in a corpus.

short: The instantaneous rate of change of a function with respect to a single input variable.
eli5: Looking at a hill right under your feet to tell whether stepping right goes uphill or downhill and how steep it is.
example: Measuring how much prediction error changes if one neural network weight nudges up slightly.

short: A vector of partial derivatives pointing in the direction of steepest increase of a multi-variable function.
eli5: A compass arrow on a mountain slope that points straight uphill—so walking the opposite way takes you downhill fastest.
example: Computing how all millions of weights should shift together to lower training loss.

short: Techniques like PCA or UMAP that compress high-dimensional data into fewer dimensions while preserving key structure.
eli5: Taking a 3D sculpture and casting a shadow on a wall so you can still recognize its shape in 2D.
example: Projecting 1536-dimensional text embeddings onto a 2D scatter map for visual inspection.
